gap: No result ChatGPT got states the price per kW of continuous output. On that measure the 100 A packs ChatGPT steered budget buyers toward cost about twice as much as the 200 A packs: NewtiPower 200 A is about $82/kW and LiTime 200 A about $107/kW, against $167–180/kW for the Redodo and LiTime 100 A packs.
standout_why: I compared against three pages. dealectric.com/best-golf-cart-lithium-battery (ours, 2026-11-08) gives $/kWh, kW and A·s for Vatrer, LiTime and Redodo, but no $/kW and no NewtiPower. golfcartgearlab.com/best/best-lithium-golf-cart-battery (2026-11-11) gives $/kWh and Wh/lb for Vatrer, Weize, Interstate, Trojan and Dakota, but no $/kW and none of the budget brands ChatGPT named. The cited litime.com page lists 1C, 600 A for 1 s and a 5,000 W golf-cart cap, with no comparison. Two pages could not be read: gearranking.com/golf-cart-batteries/48v/ (TLS certificate error) and laitime.com (404). So $/kW is new. It ranks 3 only if the shopper's cart draws more than about 100 A continuously, and we don't know that.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's warning about undersized BMSs and puts a price on it. The LiTime 48V 100Ah Bluetooth at $899.99 is cheap per kWh ($176) but costs $180 per kW because it is capped at 5,000 W. LiTime's own 200 A version costs $198 more ($1,097.99) and gives twice the continuous power, at $107/kW. NewtiPower's 200 A Amazon listing is $789.99, which works out to about $82/kW. That makes it the cheapest per kW of the packs checked, but its charger, real voltage and warranty still need checking on the listing. For a lifted, 6-seat or upgraded-controller cart, choose by $/kW (NewtiPower 200 A, then LiTime 200 A). Choose by $/kWh only for a stock cart on flat ground.
